2_motivation: The batch-1 seed direction (§12.1: "all-pairs fidelity training … `mf_field/akash/models/mf_fno_allpairs`") is scored by the websearcher as **`preempted-but-MF-composition-open`**, open only as "**Not found published**: (i) **all ordered pairs** (not just adjacent) as a data-amplification augmentation, (ii) with a **single shared** network rather than one net per level, (iii) at **N_hf = 5** on the `li2022ifc` Poisson ladder." Reading that family against the data shows it *cannot be tested on this ladder as built*: `ifc_poisson`'s four fidelity levels are **not sample-aligned** (verified: `np.allclose(X8[:5], X64)` → `False`, max |diff| 0.581; same for every other pair), while `build_pairs` pairs `cond_by_fid[s][:n]` with `field_by_fid[t][:n]` and the finetune stage pairs LF conditions with HF fields. Every cross-fidelity row and the whole finetune stage therefore associate parameters with fields from *different* samples — which is exactly what its 0.4657 nRMSE on `ifc_poisson` (vs the champion's 0.0488) and 0.1457 on `ifc_heat` in `akash/results/bench_full_metrics.csv` predict, on precisely the two non-aligned datasets, while it wins the aligned npz datasets. This card fixes the correspondence and makes the pair set the measured variable, following the websearcher's directive "**Design the pair set as the actual variable.**"
3_description:
family `mf_fno_ladder` in the worktree, vendored from `akash/models/mf_fno_allpairs` + `akash/common/backbone.py` (SMOKE hyperparameters identical to the anchor family: hidden 64, blocks 4, modes_cap 12, batch 16, lr_pretrain 1e-3, lr_finetune 3e-4, wd 1e-5, clip 1.0). Rows `(cond = [X, f_src, f_tgt]) → Y@(64,64)`, with `f = (log fid − log 8)/(log 64 − log 8)`. **Correction**: cross-pair rows take the condition vector from the **target** fidelity's own sample list (a no-op on aligned datasets, a fix on the ifc ladder), and **self pairs (f,f) are included** so the 100/50/20/5 ladder rows all enter training. Stage 1: joint training on the arm's row set, 200 epochs. Stage 2 (identical in every arm): HF finetune on the 5 rows `(X^{(64)}, f_src=0, f_tgt=1) → Y^{(64)}`, 200 epochs. Eval query `(X_test, f_src=0, f_tgt=1)`.
Four arms via `MFFP_LADDER_MODE`:

| arm | levels | tags | rows | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `two_level` | {8,64} | self ×2 + (8,64) | 110 | information-content control ≈ the champion |
| `adjacent` | all 4 | self ×4 + (8,16),(16,32),(32,64) | 250 | published cascade structure |
| `allpairs` | all 4 | self ×4 + all 6 ordered (s<t) | 280 | **primary** — the open composition |
| `legacy_pairing` | all 4 | same rows, cross rows source-indexed | 280 | isolates the correspondence defect |

Two build traps recorded for the builder/reviewer: (1) `score_panel._run_one` derives `out_json`/`ckpt_dir` from `(family_dir.name, dataset, epochs, seed)` only — the arm is invisible, and the base resume logic would silently reload another arm's `last.pt`; the checkpoint key **must** include the arm and the job script **must** export a per-arm `ROUND1_EVAL_RESULTS`. (2) The family must be *vendored*, not imported from `akash/**` via `parents[2]`, both because akash is a guarded read-only surface and because `code_hash` would not see the imported code. The result JSON `extra` also records (score-neutrally) the per-pair `max |X^{(s)}[:n] − X^{(t)}[:n]|` alignment measurement and the per-arm row counts.
4_expected_result: metric = `ifc_poisson` test nRMSE → skill vs paper bar 0.036 (ADR 0002), mean over seeds {0,1,2}. Anchor = **1.5656 [1.4562, 1.6961]** (nRMSE ≈ 0.0564). Predictions: `allpairs` **skill 1.15–1.40 (nRMSE 0.041–0.050)**, point estimate ≈1.28 → Δ ≈ **−0.29 skill vs anchor**, just above the **0.2399** floor; `adjacent` within the floor of `allpairs`; `two_level` ≈ anchor (1.4–1.7); `legacy_pairing` **≥ 3.0 skill (nRMSE ≥ 0.108)**, ≈6× the floor away from the anchor. Mechanism: the 32² level's 20 samples are the only supervision besides the 5 HF samples covering spectral modes 4–12 (an 8² field lifted to 64² carries content only to mode ≈4; the FNO represents 12), and the 16² level adds 50 more rows. Stated plainly: the anchor comparison is *marginal* against the floor at this tier; the robust part of the card is the three internal contrasts (same code, same seeds, same hyperparameters). Wall-clock: batch 0 ran `ifc_poisson` @200 epochs in 0.78–0.98 min, so 4 arms ≈ 15 min/seed → `--time=01:00:00` is ample.
expected_falsification: Falsified if the full-ladder all-ordered-pairs arm fails to beat the two-level arm on `ifc_poisson` by more than the certified noise floor — mean skill over seeds {0,1,2} improving by ≤ 0.240 skill units (≤ 0.00864 nRMSE) — which would mean the intermediate fidelities (16², 32²) carry no usable information for HF reconstruction at N_hf = 5 beyond what the 8²→64² transfer already exploits.

Per reviewer note S4, legacy_pairing here keeps the corrected HF finetune and the added self pairs, so this delta isolates the CROSS-ROW CORRESPONDENCE ONLY; it must not be reported as the base family's 0.4657 in akash/results/bench_full_metrics.csv.

contrasts.name: allpairs vs two_level (does more ladder help once correspondence is fixed?)
contrasts.direction: allpairs WORSE (higher skill) by 2.9601 - OPPOSITE to the card's prediction
contrasts.reading: two_level (110 rows, {8,64} only) is the best arm of the four. Adding the 16^2/32^2 levels to the joint stage did not merely fail to help, it roughly DOUBLED test rel-L2 (0.1027 -> 0.2093). Descriptive within-seed check on the 128 per-sample rel_l2 values from the family JSONs: two_level beats allpairs on 125/128 test samples (allpairs better on only 3), median paired diff +0.0673, and the allpairs/two_level mean-error ratio is 2.02 / 1.97 / 1.92 / 2.10 across quartiles of two_level's own error magnitude - i.e. a near-UNIFORM ~2x multiplicative degradation, not a tail or outlier effect.

contrasts.name: allpairs vs adjacent (all ordered pairs vs the published adjacent cascade)
contrasts.reading: Exceeds the 0.23991 floor by 0.00199 skill units (0.8%). At single seed with no CI this is NOT a resolvable effect - treat as at-the-floor / noise-compatible. The three extra pair types (8->32, 8->64, 16->64) buy nothing measurable once both arms carry all four levels.

contrasts.name: adjacent vs two_level (auxiliary: does the published cascade help?)
contrasts.reading: The degradation tracks the presence of the intermediate levels in the joint stage, not the pair-set richness: both four-level arms (adjacent 6.055, allpairs 5.813) sit ~2x worse than the two-level arm, and they differ from each other only at the floor.

amplitude_domination_caveat.source: code-reviewer note S2 (state/s1_poisson/review_B1.md), measured on the real data before launch
amplitude_domination_caveat.statement: Per-fidelity max|Y| = 0.0773 / 0.0237 / 0.0069 / 0.00184 at fid 8/16/32/64 (42x spread); the stage-1 scaler max|Y_all| = 0.077146 is IDENTICAL across all four arms (so it is not an arm confound), but the joint stage's MSE is amplitude-dominated by the 8^2 rows and stage 2 renormalizes by scaler_hf = 0.001836. Consequence for interpretation: the C2a/C3 result is NOT licensed to be read as 'the 16^2/32^2 levels carry no usable information for HF reconstruction'. What is measured is that adding those levels TO THIS JOINT-STAGE LOSS, under this amplitude weighting and this shared-scaler normalization, degrades the HF query by ~2x. Whether the intermediate fidelities are uninformative or merely down-weighted into irrelevance (and their rows acting as a distractor/capacity tax on a single shared net) is not separated by this card. This is the first thing part 6 should test.
amplitude_domination_caveat.additional_caveat_S3: The minibatch generator is torch.Generator().manual_seed(0), seed-independent (reviewer S3), so any future seeds 1-2 vary only via init/CUDA nondeterminism and their CI will be optimistically narrow.

vs_anchor.direction: allpairs WORSE than anchor by 4.2476 skill units
vs_anchor.note: All four arms are worse than the anchor, the best (two_level, 2.853) by 1.287 skill units = 5.4x the floor. This is CONTEXT, not the card's experiment: this family is not the champion and the card's own hypothesis is the three internal contrasts (same code, same seed, same hyperparameters). The card predicted allpairs at skill 1.15-1.40 (nRMSE 0.041-0.050); the measurement is 5.813 (nRMSE 0.2093), ~4.5x the predicted skill and outside the prediction interval by a factor of >4.

5_actual_result.cratered_basis: Cratered rule applied to the PRIMARY arm allpairs only (recipe.env._primary_arm; reviewer S4). Threshold = cratered_skill_factor 1.5 x anchor 1.5656334 = 2.3484501. allpairs = 5.8131983 > 2.3484501 (2.48x the threshold) => CRATERED. Independently, the falsification clause fired decisively (see falsification_verdict). No crash occurred - the job exited 0 on all four arms. legacy_pairing (8.3619) is also above the threshold, which is the PREDICTED and BY-DESIGN result for the negative control and is not a cratering event. adjacent (6.0551) and two_level (2.8531) also exceed 1.5x anchor, but the rule is scoped to the primary arm. Under ADR 0004 there is no proceed_to_seeds_1_2 branch: seeds 1-2 run only in the end-of-round top-3 confirmation, for which this card is not a candidate.
5_actual_result.falsification_basis: Clause quoted verbatim: 'Falsified if the full-ladder all-ordered-pairs arm fails to beat the two-level arm on ifc_poisson by more than the certified noise floor - mean skill over seeds {0,1,2} improving by <= 0.240 skill units (<= 0.00864 nRMSE) - which would mean the intermediate fidelities (16^2, 32^2) carry no usable information for HF reconstruction at N_hf = 5 beyond what the 8^2->64^2 transfer already exploits.' Deciding numbers (seed 0, 200 ep): allpairs skill 5.813198 (nRMSE 0.209275) vs two_level skill 2.853063 (nRMSE 0.102710). The improvement is -2.960135 skill units (-0.106565 nRMSE), i.e. allpairs is WORSE, so it does not merely fail to improve by more than 0.240 - it regresses by 12.3x the floor. FALSIFIED. Two honesty qualifiers: (i) provisional-single-seed - the clause is written on the mean over seeds {0,1,2} and only seed 0 was run per ADR 0004, so this is a seed-0 point estimate; the magnitude (12.3x the certified 3-seed floor, plus 125/128 per-sample paired wins for two_level) makes a seed-driven reversal implausible but not formally excluded; (ii) the clause's stated MEANING ('the intermediate fidelities carry no usable information') is NOT established - see amplitude_domination_caveat. The measurement falsifies the card's prediction; the mechanistic gloss in the clause is over-claimed by the caveat and must be re-tested in part 6.

6_analysis.protocol: Three probe turns, all in <worktree>/scratchpad, no SLURM, no worktree code edits, nothing recomputed by hand (every nRMSE via ${ROUND_ROOT}/eval/nrmse.py, every dataset read via ${ROUND_ROOT}/eval/panel_data.py). Turn 1 = data-level ladder diagnostic (reanalysis_turn_1.py -> turn1_out/turn1_results.json). Turn 2 = error decomposition of the four shipped preds_test.npz + f_tgt sweep on the four shipped last.pt (reanalysis_turn_2.py -> turn2_out/turn2_results.json). Turn 3 = a re-normalized ablation at REDUCED CAPACITY (hidden 16 / 2 blocks / modes 8, joint 30 ep, finetune 200 ep, 1 CPU core; production config costs 6.58 s/minibatch = ~6.6 h/arm on this node) (reanalysis_turn_3.py -> turn3_out/*.json). EVERY turn-3 number is a scratchpad proxy and none of them is or may become a card number. Turn results: scratchpad/reanalysis_turn_{1,2,3}_results.md.
findings: T1 - the ifc_poisson ladder's four levels differ by a clean discretization scale law, not by information: per-level RMS|Y| = 0.0245499 / 0.0056065 / 0.0013362 / 0.00032434 at fid 8/16/32/64, consecutive ratios 4.3788 / 4.1957 / 4.1198 (i.e. ~h^2), total spread 75.7x in RMS and 42.1x in max|Y| (turn1_results.json:amplitude_law).

T1 - after nearest-condition matching (the levels are NOT index-aligned), every ordered level pair agrees in SHAPE: rel-L2 after one optimal global gain = 0.14219 (8->16), 0.17583 (8->32), 0.17439 (8->64), 0.11086 (16->32), 0.14163 (16->64), 0.11170 (32->64), with mean Pearson r 0.9412-0.9885 and min r 0.8488. The fitted gains (0.22887, 0.053096, 0.013566) reproduce the amplitude law (turn1_results.json:cross_level_consistency_train).

T1 - condition-space coverage is not the failure: all four level clouds and the 128 test conditions span the same 5-D box (per-dim min 0.101-0.123, max 0.866-0.900); mean scaled NN distance from the test conditions is 1.0067 to fid 8, 1.2145 to fid 16, 1.4523 to fid 32 and 2.0726 to the 5 HF training points; frac_exact = 0 everywhere. The intermediate levels add 70 parameter points that are CLOSER to the test distribution than the HF training points are (turn1_results.json:condition_coverage).

T1 - a training-free 'matched-level' predictor (nearest-condition sample at level f, bilinearly upsampled, times ONE gain calibrated on the 5 HF train samples) scores nRMSE 0.24828 from the 8^2 level alone, vs 76.600 for the same fields uncalibrated - a ~300x error swing that is pure amplitude. Reference points: zero predictor 1.0, HF-train-mean predictor 0.40343 (turn1_results.json:matched_level_predictor_on_test).

T1 - adding the intermediate levels does NOT squeeze the HF rows out of the joint loss: normalized target-energy share of the fid-64 rows is 0.0011158 in two_level and 0.0018028 in allpairs, i.e. slightly LARGER in the arm that lost; the intermediate rows take their ~19% share out of the 8^2 rows (turn1_results.json:joint_loss_energy_share_shared_scaler).

T2 - the four-level arms' extra error is amplitude, not structure: fraction of squared test error explained by a per-sample scalar gain = 0.3088 (two_level), 0.7473 (allpairs), 0.8006 (adjacent), 0.7849 (legacy_pairing). Correcting each sample with its own oracle gain takes allpairs 0.209275 -> 0.089110 and two_level 0.102710 -> 0.078814, collapsing the headline 2.04x gap to 1.13x (turn2_results.json:prediction_decomposition).

T2 - a single GLOBAL oracle gain changes nothing (allpairs 0.209275 -> 0.210222), so the miscalibration is per-sample, and shape agreement is nearly arm-independent (mean Pearson r 0.98300 / 0.97817 / 0.97377 / 0.97376) (turn2_results.json:prediction_decomposition).

T2 - the degradation is concentrated in the lowest spectral band, which carries 99.78% of the target energy: band-0 relative error 0.0740 (two_level) vs 0.1736 (allpairs), a 2.346x penalty, against 1.26-1.47x in the five higher bands. This contradicts the card's part-4 mechanism argument, which located the value of the 32^2 level in spectral modes 4-12 (turn2_results.json:spectral_bands).

T2 - the arms differ only in the condition-dependent part of the field. Across-sample variance retained (var(pred)/var(target)): two_level 0.8574, allpairs 0.4408, adjacent 0.4206, legacy_pairing 0.2652; nRMSE of the mean-removed fields 0.30008 / 0.57137 / 0.58106 / 0.78749. All four arms reproduce the mean HF field equally well (corr >= 0.99985 with the HF-train mean). The ranking by retained conditional variance is exactly the arm ranking (turn2_results.json:collapse_check).

T2 - after stage 2 no arm's network encodes the ladder's gain law: output RMS relative to f_tgt=1 across f_tgt in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1} is 2.851/2.155/1.515/1.0 (two_level), 3.356/2.168/1.457/1.0 (allpairs), vs the data's 75.69/17.29/4.12/1.0. Stage 2 renormalizes by scaler_hf = 0.0018357 against stage 1's 0.0772146 (ratio 42.06) and drags the whole f_tgt axis with it (turn2_results.json:ftgt_sweep_on_final_ckpt).

T3 [REDUCED-CAPACITY PROXY, scratchpad only] validity gate: the proxy reproduces the production ORDERING with attenuated magnitude - allpairs/shared 0.214313 vs two_level/shared 0.183150 = 1.17x worse (production 2.04x) (turn3_out/*__shared__j30__*_s0.json).

T3 [PROXY] the optimization-budget hypothesis is falsified: at a matched step budget (allpairs 216 joint minibatches vs two_level 210) allpairs scores 0.215912, statistically indistinguishable from its 540-minibatch run (0.214313) and still worse than two_level at 210 (0.183150) (turn3_out/allpairs__shared__j12__*_s0.json).

T3 [PROXY] the decisive intervention: dividing each row by its OWN level's max|Y| instead of the shared max|Y_all| takes allpairs from 0.214313 to 0.087352 (2.45x better), making it the best run of the grid - 1.69x better than two_level/per_level (0.147214) and 2.10x better than the best shared-scaler arm. The same change helps two_level by only 1.24x, i.e. the benefit scales with how much of the ladder the arm pools (turn3_out/*__per_level__*_s0.json).

T3 [PROXY] the turn-2 mechanism markers move with the intervention: for allpairs, shared -> per_level gives across-sample variance retained 0.31958 -> 1.27758, Pearson r 0.97481 -> 0.98772, structure-only nRMSE 0.098750 -> 0.059152.

T3 - HONESTY: the seed-1 replication is incomplete. two_level/shared/seed1 = 0.151104 (so the proxy baseline spans 0.1511-0.1832 across two seeds, +/-10%), but both allpairs seed-1 runs were killed at the 1200 s cap (exit=124) when the login node's load average reached 20.6. The seed-0 grid is the evidence; the 2.45x intervention effect is ~an order of magnitude larger than the observed baseline seed spread, but no CI is claimed.
interpretation: MECHANISM (high confidence; supported by T1 amplitude law + T2 A/C/D + the T3 intervention): the ladder arms fail by AMPLITUDE-CHANNEL CAPTURE. On ifc_poisson the field's magnitude is the dominant signal (99.78% of target energy in the lowest radial band) and it is driven by two things at once - the fidelity tag (42-76x across levels) and the condition vector (the sample-to-sample variation the model is actually asked to predict). Because stage 1 normalizes every level by one scalar taken from the coarsest, largest-amplitude level, the f_tgt gain law becomes the larger regularity and captures the network's amplitude degree of freedom; the 5-row stage-2 finetune then has to multiply the output by 42x at f_tgt=1 and does so GLOBALLY (T2 D), yielding a predictor with the right shape (r ~ 0.974) and roughly half the required conditional variance (0.44 vs two_level's 0.86). More levels in the joint stage = a wider gain law to carry = more capture = more collapse, which is exactly the observed arm ranking.

COROLLARY (high confidence): the pair set was never the operative variable. The card measured a level-set effect through a normalization defect. allpairs vs adjacent differ by 1.008x the noise floor (card part 5, C2b) because they pool the same four levels; two_level wins only because it pools the fewest.

COROLLARY (medium-high confidence, proxy-based): the ladder is NOT worthless at N_hf = 5 - under per-level normalization the full four-level pair set is the best configuration tested, beating the two-level control by 1.69x in the same proxy. The open composition the websearcher scored as unpublished (all ordered pairs, one shared net, N_hf = 5) has NOT been fairly tested by this card; it was tested through a broken normalization.

SCOPE (medium confidence): the defect is dataset-shaped. It requires a large per-level amplitude spread under a shared scaler. Datasets whose levels are already comparable in magnitude (the aligned npz_l panel members) would show little of it - consistent with the base family mf_fno_allpairs winning the npz datasets and losing on the two ifc datasets (card part 2), where BOTH defects (cross-row correspondence and the amplitude law) live.

NOT SUPPORTED: the card part-4 spectral mechanism ('the 32^2 level's 20 samples are the only supervision covering spectral modes 4-12'). The value at stake is in the lowest band; the four-level arms lose 2.35x there and only 1.26-1.47x in the higher bands, and all arms under-predict high-band energy regardless of level set.
6_analysis.falsification_postmortem: The clause fired correctly as a PREDICTION test and incorrectly as a MECHANISM claim, and both halves are now explained. (i) The prediction ('allpairs beats two_level by more than 0.240 skill') failed because the card assumed the joint stage's extra levels would act as spectral supervision, whereas in this family they act as an amplitude-gain-law learning task that competes with the condition-dependent amplitude the model must actually predict; the observable is a 2.04x uniform multiplicative degradation (125/128 per-sample wins for two_level) whose ~75% is per-sample gain error and which disappears (2.04x -> 1.13x) under a per-sample oracle gain. (ii) The clause's stated meaning - 'the intermediate fidelities carry no usable information for HF reconstruction at N_hf = 5' - is FALSE. Turn 1 shows the 16^2/32^2 levels carry the HF field's shape at Pearson r >= 0.94 (rel-L2 <= 0.18 after one gain) at 70 parameter points that are closer in condition space to the test distribution than the 5 HF training points are; turn 3's per-level-normalized proxy shows those same rows becoming the best predictor in the grid (allpairs 0.087352 vs two_level 0.147214). The correct postmortem sentence is: the intermediate fidelities are informative, and the family's single shared stage-1 target scaler converted that information into a 42x nuisance gain law that captured the network's amplitude channel. Reviewer note S2 anticipated exactly this and was right to insist the null not be read as an information claim.
surprises: The 42x per-level spread is not an artifact of a few outliers but an exact ~h^2 scale law (consecutive RMS ratios 4.379 / 4.196 / 4.120), i.e. a completely predictable, removable nuisance - and it was being fed to a single shared scaler.

A per-sample oracle gain closes 88% of the card's headline gap (2.04x -> 1.13x). The four arms had learned almost the same function up to per-sample scale; the card's measured variable was calibration, not composition.

All four arms reproduce the mean HF field to corr >= 0.99985 and differ ONLY in retained conditional variance (0.86 / 0.44 / 0.42 / 0.27). The mean field alone already scores nRMSE 0.40343 and the primary arm scores 0.20928 - i.e. the primary arm is only ~1.9x better than a constant predictor.

A training-free nearest-condition matched-8^2 predictor with one calibration gain scores nRMSE 0.24828, better than three of the four trained arms (allpairs 0.20928 is the only arm that beats it, and only by 1.19x). That is a cheap, brutal baseline this stream should carry forward.

After the finetune, no arm's network encodes more than a 3.5x f_tgt gain response against the data's 75.7x - the joint stage's learned level law is essentially destroyed by stage 2, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that stage 1 and stage 2 are fighting over the same amplitude degree of freedom.

The intervention REVERSES the sign of the card's central contrast in the proxy: per-level normalization makes the full ladder 1.69x BETTER than the two-level control, where the shared scaler made it 1.17x worse (2.04x in production).

7_gap_and_future.open_question: Does the per-level target normalization survive at production capacity, and does the resulting full-ladder model beat anything that matters? Turn 3's proxy (hidden 16 / 2 blocks / modes 8, joint 30 ep, 1 CPU core) shows per-level normalization taking allpairs from 0.214313 to 0.087352 and past two_level/per_level (0.147214) - but the proxy's own baseline gap is attenuated (1.17x vs production's 2.04x), the two allpairs seed-1 runs were killed at the 1200 s cap, and even the best proxy number is far from the batch-0 anchor (mf_fno_transfer_film, skill 1.5656 = nRMSE 0.05636). Three things are unresolved and separable: (i) does the fix reproduce at hidden 64 / 4 blocks / modes 12, 200/200 epochs, 3 seeds; (ii) once the amplitude nuisance is removed, does the FULL ladder beat the TWO-LEVEL control by more than the 0.23991 floor - i.e. is the websearcher's open composition (all ordered pairs, one shared net, N_hf=5) actually worth anything; (iii) does any of it clear the anchor, or is this whole family structurally ~2-4x off the champion for reasons unrelated to the ladder? Note the brutal context: a training-free nearest-condition matched-8^2 predictor with one calibration gain already scores 0.24828, beating three of the four arms.
7_gap_and_future.next_direction: s1_poisson batch 2 should be a MODEL card that re-runs this exact experiment with the target normalization as the measured variable and the pair set held fixed - the inverse of B1's design. Concretely: same vendored family, one new env knob (e.g. MFFP_LADDER_SCALER in {shared, per_level}) whose only effect is dividing each stage-1 row by its own level's max|Y| instead of max|Y_all| (a ~3-line change; the diff is in scratchpad/reanalysis_turn_3.py), 2x2 arms {two_level, allpairs} x {shared, per_level} at production tier (hidden 64 / 4 blocks / modes 12, 200 joint + 200 finetune, seed 0 per ADR 0004). Predictions to write into part 4: shared arms reproduce B1 (two_level ~0.103, allpairs ~0.209); allpairs/per_level lands at or below two_level/per_level. Write the falsification clause on the NORMALIZATION contrast (allpairs/per_level vs allpairs/shared) rather than on the pair set, and add a second clause on the composition question (allpairs/per_level vs two_level/per_level) so the two are not conflated again - that conflation is exactly what made B1's clause unfalsifiable-as-worded. Carry three reference lines in the card: the anchor 1.5656, the matched-8^2-level training-free floor 0.24828, and the HF-train-mean predictor 0.40343. Cheap and worth adding as a third arm if budget allows: keep the per-level scaler but ALSO scale the stage-2 finetune consistently (already implied) and log the f_tgt output sweep, so the amplitude-channel-capture story is measured directly rather than inferred. Wall clock: B1 ran 4 arms in 4.45 min on one H100, so a 4-6 arm sweep is <10 min/seed. If batch 2 confirms the fix and still loses to the anchor, s1 should stop optimizing this family and instead ask why the anchor's transfer recipe beats a ladder that provably contains more information (see the matched-level ceiling).
7_gap_and_future.cross_stream_notes: 1) SHARED-SCALER TRAP, applies to any stream pooling fidelity levels in one loss: ifc_poisson's levels differ by a clean ~h^2 amplitude law spanning 75.7x in RMS (4.379 / 4.196 / 4.120 consecutively). Any family that normalizes pooled multi-level targets by one scalar is asking the network to learn that law along its fidelity axis; the observable signature is right shape (Pearson r ~ 0.97) + collapsed conditional variance (0.44 of target) + ~75% of squared error removable by a per-sample gain. Verified NOT present on sharp__allen_cahn_2d (index-aligned, RMS spread 1.00x), so this is dataset-shaped - check before assuming. Run tools/ladder_level_diagnostic.py. 2) DON'T ATTRIBUTE AN nRMSE GAP TO ARCHITECTURE UNTIL YOU'VE SPLIT IT: on this card a per-sample oracle gain shrank a 2.04x arm gap to 1.13x. tools/field_error_decomposition.py does this in seconds from a preds npz. 3) DUMP PREDICTIONS: this card's whole part 6 was possible only because the builder added a score-neutral np.savez of (pred, target, work_grid) beside the checkpoint (models_r1/mf_fno_ladder/smoke_eval.py:462). Every family should do it; it costs nothing and cannot be recovered afterwards. 4) CHEAP FLOORS: on ifc_poisson, a nearest-condition matched-8^2 predictor with one calibration gain scores nRMSE 0.24828 and the HF-train-mean field scores 0.40343 - three of B1's four trained arms lose to the former. Streams should quote a training-free floor next to their skill numbers. 5) ifc_poisson's fidelity levels are NOT index-aligned (max cond diff 0.58-0.74 across all six pairs) - any family constructing cross-level rows by index is training on mismatched (parameters, field) pairs; B1 measured that defect at 2.549 skill units (10.6x the floor).
